invitations.title: Across the table
invitations.brief: Could you make something low for the middle of the table? Eight of us will be talking across it all evening.

bands.note: Everyone could see everyone. Halfway through, someone moved the bread basket just to get a better look at it.
It sat in the middle all evening. When people leaned in to talk, a stem or two was in the way, and nobody minded.
It was too tall to talk across, so we moved it to the sideboard. People kept getting up to go and look at it.

invitations.title: Above the sink
invitations.brief: It's for the windowsill above the sink. The glass is right behind it and the tap is just in front, so it can't be deep. Wide is fine.

bands.note: It fits the sill exactly. In the mornings the light comes through it from behind.
One stem rests against the glass and has left a little mark on the window. I've decided I like it.
It was too deep for the sill, so it lives on the kitchen table now. That turns out to suit it.

invitations.title: Coming home
invitations.brief: It goes on a low chest by the front door. The door opens on the left. I'd like it to turn toward whoever comes in.

bands.note: When I come in, it's already turned toward me. My neighbour stopped in the doorway the first time she saw it.
It stands quite straight, as if it's waiting to see who it will be. I like that more than I expected.
It leans away from the door, toward the window. Visitors look where it looks, so now everyone notices the garden.
